notes.title: Small free content update
notes.content:
While I am currently quite busy with the development of my second game Card Coder, I did take some time to create a small content update for JOY OF PROGRAMMING.

In particular, this update includes two new levels in the Driving category where you have to setup speed traps with the help of a RangeFinder or a SmartCamera respectively.



And if a car is too fast, this is how you handle that situation:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43325028/960e3d7646ce2ae6f80150525a57398debd0257e.gif"]

notes.title: JOY OF PROGRAMMING 1.0
notes.content:
After one exciting year in Early Access, I am very pleased (and a little proud) to announce the 1.0 release of JOY OF PROGRAMMING and the conclusion of its Early Access phase. This does not mean 1.0 will be the final update. On the contrary: I plan to support JOY OF PROGRAMMING for the foreseeable future and add new levels whenever I have ideas for new challenges. Of course, I also hope the 1.0 release will bring in some new players and our little community will grow with more user made levels (check out the level editor after you're comfortable with the game itself)!

I think it is more important than ever to deepen and widen your programming skills, and game-based learning is great opportunity to do just that.

Happy Coding!

Full changelog over the last year until today:
[code]version 1.0.0
- Added "tinygrad" (https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad) to third party modules for deep learning
- Increase virtual RAM upgrades (64->128, 128->256, 256->1024)
- Added new machine: VacuumRobot, automatically cleans up all objects with tag "Dirt".
- Added two new Machine Learning levels: Image Classification and Coin Detection
- Added two new Smart Home Levels: VacuumRobot0 and VacuumRobot1
- Improved documentation for several machines

version 0.9.0
- Added a new level:
  - SQL Database (Machine Learning category)
- Preparations for 1.0 release
  - Removed "Beta Map" feature.
  - Cleaned up some obsolete UI
- Linux/Proton support: Please use Proton Experimental. All levels (including image processing levels) now work correctly under Proton Experimental (but not under Proton 9.03).
- Known issues:
  - Localization: While the UI and the tutorials are fully localized in different languages, most other levels do not support localization. These are created with the included level editor which does not support easy localization. Unfortunately, this cannot be easily amended and will not change in the upcoming 1.0 release.

- replaced python.exe with pythonw.exe. The background python process is now invisible.

- Fixed typo in Track Follower level.

notes.title: Update #15 and 1.0 Announcement
notes.content:
Update 15 brings JOY OF PROGRAMMING to version 0.9.0. This update is mostly a maintenance patch for the upcoming 1.0 release and the end of Early Access.

JOY OF PROGRAMMING 1.0 will be released on January 18th 2025 and leave Early Access. This is almost exactly one year after the initial Early Access launch in January 2024. A lot has happened since then and I can confidently say that the game is in much better shape today and contains a lot more content. So a big thank you to every Early Access player and in particular to everyone who has been reporting bugs, making suggestions or helping others in the game's discord channel. 
To manage expectations for the 1.0 release: There is no big surprise or new feature planned. Rather it will be a content update similar to the previous updates, meaning new levels, fixes and improvements. 

Now back to this update! To shorten the wait, this update does include 1 new level that is a little different from what you've seen so far. Hope you'll like it.

Happy Coding!

Full changelog:
[code]
- Added a new level:
  - SQL Database (Machine Learning category)
- Preparations for 1.0 release
  - Removed "Beta Map" feature.
  - Cleaned up some obsolete UI
- Linux/Proton support: Please use Proton Experimental. All levels (including image processing levels) now work correctly under Proton Experimental (but not under Proton 9.03).
- Known issues:
  - Localization: While the UI and the tutorials are fully localized in different languages, most other levels do not support localization. These are created with the included level editor which does not support easy localization. Unfortunately, this cannot be easily amended and will not change in the upcoming 1.0 release.
[/code]

notes.title: The Creative Freedom
notes.content:
Not all environments in JOY OF PROGRAMMING are tough to crack programming challenges. Sometimes it's all about letting your own creativity take over. Here are some upcoming levels to show you what I mean:

Let there be sound
Create some procedural melodies or beats, similar to how DAWs and MIDI sequencers work. But use the full power of Python and be creative (please note that I have almost zero knowledge about music theory and cannot play a single instrument. I can whistle though!).
[previewyoutube=vPYI9YPp3gg;full][/previewyoutube]

Stackenblocken
Okay, that word does not exit, but who doesn't love to stack some blocks on top of each other? You can do just that and create some nice, minimalistic voxel art.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43325028/c66e4a7aaaced31bf3659a24eeb4530d994494f4.gif

Of course it's not difficult to imagine using this technique in some 3D-printing related levels.

RGBW-LEDs
You can do some really fun stuff with programmable RGBW-LED strips in real life. Obviously we need those in JOY OF PROGRAMMING as well!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43325028/3e2dee46846350e18879b33a2ac93c5199ea4014.gif

One challenge I have in mind is creating an ambient lighting setup, such that the LED strip projects colors corresponding to the current TV image (like those nice, but expensive TVs with ambient lighting).

Other Updates
I'm preparing for another playtest in June. This time directly on Steam, though all details will be shared via our Discord as before. I'm also in the process of preparing an open-source release of the Python wrapper for JOY OF PROGRAMMING. That way you can already glimpse at the programming interface before the game's release and if you are a seasoned Python developer you can even directly contribute to the interface. More on this in the next devlog!

Happy Coding!

notes.title: Devlog #4
notes.content:
Most scenarios in JOY OF PROGRAMMING as of right now consist of a fixed set of programmable machines and you are tasked with writing their code. However, I implemented a sandbox / building mode quite some time ago. It basically allows you to unlock different machines and place them in a level freely  (with some budget limitations) to solve some open-ended task:

To be honest, I have not yet designed too many levels around this mechanic that I am truly happy with. So this devlog is a little different in so far, as I'd like to get your feedback and your ideas on this:
What kind of open-ended scenario / sandbox environment would you like to see, where you can buy, place and program different machines freely?

notes.title: Devlog #3
notes.content:
Currently I'm working on a new category of levels based around breaking ciphers and brute-forcing passwords. Here is a sneak preview into one of them.

What's my PIN again?
You forgot the code for your safe (of course it's your safe, you wouldn't want to open someone else's safe, right? Right?). All you remember is it was 3 digits. That's 1000 possible solutions. Easy but not exactly fun to try out all combinations by hand. A simple brute-force script can automate that and open the lock in a couple of seconds (because you are limited in the number of combinations you can enter per second). However, meet the miracle PinHacker device:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43325028/eaabc134e754c59419aa1d6af291bf205919ca59.gif

It can tell you if the pin you entered is greater than or less than the true pin. Could you come up with a more efficient search strategy using this information?

Python Tips and Tricks
The seemingly simple "+" operator has quite a lot of different uses in Python:

 Add numeric values [code]x = 5 +3[/code]
 Concatenate strings [code]print("x is: " + str(x))[/code]
 Merge lists [code]long_list = [1,2,3] + [4,5,6][/code]

This is done using a principle called operator overloading.

Quiz Time
There are many possible solutions to the previous quiz. One way to simplify the code is [spoiler] to drop the len>0 expression. [code]my_name = "max"
my_age = 38
if my_age>=0 and my_name:
    print("hello there")
else:
    print("invalid")[/code][/spoiler]

Now for today's quiz, what's the output of this code (please use the [noparse][spoiler][/noparse] tag for your answer)?
[code]def clamp(x,a,b):
    if x  b:
        return b
    return x

a = 15 / 2
a = clamp(a,0,5)
print(a)[/code]

notes.title: Devlog #2
notes.content:
What is arguably the most important part of a programming game? The code editor! Modern programming requires a good IDE and not just a text editor (unless you are a VIM purist). I'm currently hard at work to give you the best possible coding experience in the integrated code editor within JOY OF PROGRAMMING. Here are some of its most useful features.

The Amazing Code Editor
Syntax Highlighting
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43325028/db095bbaad027807bec2edb94d7843a78f2e534a.jpg
Important keywords, comments, classes, functions and methods are highlighted in different colors. Eventually more color themes or custom themes will be supported.


Autocompletion / Code Hints
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43325028/4300ea5bca8ecb74c497ecba3d0f26840bca9757.gif
Maybe the most powerful feature of a good IDE is code completion. Essentially providing a list of possible tokens while you are typing. Using the power of the underlying mypy linter and it's type inference, the code editor provides you with context sensitive completion hints. So for example, if you type a dot "." after a variable pointing to a conveyor belt, you will see all member methods of the conveyor belt class.


Tooltips on Mouse Hover
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43325028/db8253d60b27cdeee698fb598f1b01a88a463126.gif
Hover the mouse for a split second over a piece of text and a helpful tooltip will pop-up providing information about the data type, usage details and sometimes example code. You can also select text within the tooltip and copy / paste it (Ctrl-C / Ctrl-V).


Other Goodies
Smaller QoL features of the code editor include undo/redo (Ctrl-Z / Ctrl-Y), changing the font size (Ctrl + mouse-wheel) and focussing entities in the 3D Viewport from the code (right click on the string name of an entity, e.g. "_entityConveyorBelt0".

Python Tips and Tricks
Python supports very flexible truth testing. If you are coming from other languages you might be used to writing your if conditions like so:
[code]some_list = [5,6,9]
if len(some_list) > 0:
    do_stuff()
[/code]
However Python supports truth testing any object. And by default, any object that reports length 0 is considered "False". So you can simplify the code above:
[code]some_list = [5,6,9]
if some_list:
    do_stuff()
[/code]
For more information have a look at the official Python documentation.

Quiz Time
The solution to the previous quiz is [spoiler]---> 8 =0 and len(my_name)>0:
    print("hello there")
else:
    print("invalid")
[/code]
Write your solutions in the comments below (consider using the [noparse][spoiler] and [code][/noparse] tags).
